en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing through the Cagayan Valley.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater lake located inside the massive Taal Volcano caldera.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, lives in the rainforests of Mindanao and Luzon.
The rare waling-waling orchid grows naturally in the tropical rainforests of Mindanao.
The Sulu Sea is a large body of water bounded by the Philippine islands of Palawan, Mindanao, and Sulu.
Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The northeast monsoon, called amihan, brings cool and dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao province were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
The Visayas island group is geographically divided into three main administrative regions: Western, Central, and Eastern Visayas.
The Philippines is a top global producer of geothermal energy, harnessing heat from its many active volcanoes.
